answer: Sybil resistance works by making identity costly through bonded sponsorship. Each new agent needs two members who stake reputation behind it as a liable anchor: if the newcomer is a duplicate, those sponsors lose bond, so endorsements stay scarce. To stop one owner splitting into many silent sybils, each registration is sealed in a shared cipher-committed log with overlapping neighbors, so a hidden cluster must act alike and any split shows. Sponsorship forms a willow of traceable branches. A mass attacker must fund real bonds and failed sponsors everywhere, making attack cost outweigh reward.
